finding.title: Pre-flight: re-ground approved findings against HEAD
finding.summary:
Pre-flight re-grounding, before ANY implementation dispatch. Re-resolve the affected_files of all 116 approved findings in approved-findings.json against the current tree at HEAD. This closes the round-3 judge classification of the phantom-drop collision (counterexample CE-002, classified residual_risk, whose tolerability rests on a measured 0-of-374 cited paths resolving — a measurement that must be re-taken because planning has been deferred past the point where phase work could move files).

The rule, exactly as the classification records it: any finding whose cited paths no longer resolve is dispositioned refuted-against-HEAD, with evidence naming the deleted path, through the one outcomes writer — it reaches .audit-tools/remediation-outcomes.json as the persisted member `refuted` via dispositionToOutcomeStatus. NO coverage join is weakened: the 26 INV-COVERAGE joins keep deriving their owned sets from approved-findings.json (the submitted set), and none is retargeted at the grounded set — retargeting would let a finding vanish from coverage by acquiring a stale path, which is the exact T-002 hole this run exists to close. Equally, a phantom path is NOT grounds to refuse the plan (that contradicts fail-9's A1 and turns one rename into a total run refusal).

The contingency is expected to be empty. If it fires, the refuted-against-HEAD record needs the widened vocabulary that item-status-partition-and-close lands in one commit (RemediationOutcomeStatus + DISPOSITION_TO_OUTCOME_STATUS + the PerFindingDisposition union at its declaration in src/remediate/state/disposition.ts) — so the disposition rides that writer rather than being invented here, and this node blocks on it instead of narrowing a join.

Output: a grounding verdict for all 116 findings (resolved / not-resolved with the offending path), and — only if any finding fails to ground — the refuted-against-HEAD records emitted through the outcomes writer. If every finding grounds, this node records the re-measurement and nothing else changes.

Traceability: this node carries no module obligations of its own. It verifies OBL-remediate-nextstep-and-final-gate-fail-9 (the phantom-drop rule the collision is against) and all 26 INV-COVERAGE obligations (the joins it must not weaken). CE-002 is carried in addresses_counterexamples where the artifact accepts it; the round-3 counterexample ids are round-scoped and the current counterexample artifact is empty, so the coverage that binds is this description plus the verification obligations above.

CDC-31 (recorded, closed): the routing closure is EMPTY across all four channels (file_scope, clause 1(a) read-only, 1(b) transient, 1(c) declared-written), so every file the design requires editing has somewhere to land under allowed_files enforcement; the closure is only meaningful when all four channels are subtracted together.

CDC-33 (recorded, economics): the round-6 repair was ~470 characters of contract text and cost +4.4KB of artifact because the shared coverage clause is paid for 26 times; this sets the price of any further contract round and argues against one.

CDC-34 (recorded, decision): PROCEED — no eighth contract round. Both refill findings are closed, no round-6-introduced defect was found, and what remains is size (CDC-21/13/33), two refinements in files item-status already owns (CDC-19/28), standing structural recommendations (CDC-08/11/22/18/27/03), and CDC-10's single owner question, now waived.

CDC-21 (recorded for between-runs, NOT implemented in this run): the coverage invariant is one 8,744-character template replicated 26 times — 57% of all invariant text. The mechanical extraction (state the rule once, carry the per-module id list as data) changes no obligation and blocks nothing now; do it before the next audit cycle, not during this implementation.

finding.title: Analyzer admission veto, scoped consent token, verified binaries
finding.summary:
Defect classes closed: The acquired-analyzer chokepoint end to end: admission, execution, output normalization, and the status vocabulary that describes a run. Makes a recorded "declined" decision a veto checked BEFORE any consent token (including for default-set candidates), scopes the consent token to the single tool it authorizes instead of accepting any non-empty string run-globally, re-verifies the cached binary's SHA256 on every execution rather than trusting filename existence in a predictable world-writable tmpdir, and replaces every success-shaped empty with an affirmation — a non-zero exit, a captured stderr, a checksum mismatch, or a malformed payload becomes a distinct classified status in the analyzer status enum, never "success" and never a bare []. Also normalizes external analyzer item paths to repo-relative at the boundary so provenance and downstream path joins survive an absolute-path emitter. Owns both of its suites: the detect() predicates must be asserted TRUE (an always-false detector currently passes the whole file) and binary acquisition needs Windows coverage, not only the linux tar path. Carries T-006 in full plus every analyzer-status finding from T-002/T-003/T-005 and the two T-001/T-007 test repairs on its own suites. Priority theme (T-006) — /design-check before reshaping the consent token.

Spec (do not restate it here): finalized_module_contracts["external-analyzer-acquisition-boundary"] — its inputs, outputs, 19 invariants, side_effects, validation_boundary, 11 failure_modes and seam_adjustments are the binding statement of what to build; the matching test specs in test_validator_plan (one per obligation) are the binding statement of how it is proven.

Invariants to make true: all 31 obligations listed in satisfies_obligations — the module contract obligation, 19 invariants (inv-1..inv-19) and 11 failure modes (fail-1..fail-11).

Write scope: src/shared/analyzerPolicy.ts, src/shared/analyzers/acquisitionEngine.ts, src/shared/analyzers/binaryAcquisition.ts, src/shared/analyzers/candidates.ts, src/shared/analyzers/normalizeExternal.ts, src/shared/analyzers/rubocop.ts, src/shared/analyzers/types.ts, tests/shared/analyzer-candidates.test.ts, tests/shared/binary-acquisition.test.ts. Nothing outside it; a change another module owns is that module's node, not this one.

Coverage join (OBL-external-analyzer-acquisition-boundary-inv-19): this module owns the terminal disposition of exactly 18 approved finding id(s), derived mechanically from file_scope joined against approved-findings.json. Every owned id must reach a terminal disposition in .audit-tools/remediation-outcomes.json through dispositionToOutcomeStatus; the join is live-derived and must not be narrowed to make it pass.

Red-green law: every spec in test_validator_plan for these obligations is red-green validated — reintroduce the named defect, confirm the test goes RED, then restore by INVERTING the edit (never `git checkout --`). A test that stays green under its own NEGATIVE mutation does not close its obligation.

Verify with: npx vitest run tests/audit/acquisition-executor.test.ts tests/audit/analyzer-consent-offer.test.ts tests/audit/graph-external-analyzers.test.ts tests/shared/analyzer-acquisition-engine.test.ts tests/shared/analyzer-candidates.test.ts tests/shared/binary-acquisition.test.ts tests/shared/candidates-safety.test.ts tests/shared/consent-token-not-persisted.test.ts, plus build/check/check:tests.

CDC-10 (advisory): the attestation half is repo law already enforced by the pre-commit hook and is NOT restated here; the /design-check half is settled by explicit owner waiver this session — Q-003's consent-token shape is accepted as decided by the loop, and the binding spec is the invariant's tool-bound property (a token authorizes exactly the one candidate it was issued for, is never persisted, and is consumed inside admitSpawn), not a re-run of the gate.

finding.title: Slice suppression without truncating the staleness walk
finding.summary:
Defect classes closed: Dependency-slice projections in the audit staleness DAG. When a projection is registered and the entry recorded a slice for the edge, an unchanged slice suppresses staleness for that artifact — but the suppression also blocks TRANSITIVE propagation to that artifact's own downstream dependents, so a genuinely stale grandchild is never refreshed. Separates "this artifact is not stale" from "stop walking here" so slice projections narrow re-derivation without truncating the DAG walk.

finding.title: Non-vacuous final gate with a durable output record
finding.summary:
Defect classes closed: The remediate next-step driver and the tool-owned final gate it consumes. A scoped-out (vacuous) final gate is consumed as a genuine green with no affirmation that any suite ran — a gate that ran zero commands becomes a first-class not-run outcome, never a pass. The final gate captures stdout/stderr and then discards it, so a run-terminating red has no diagnostic record; the output is recorded in the durable run log, as are the destructive and state-shaping diagnostics that today go only to stderr. The autonomous review gate stops overwriting the run's own canonical audit source mid-run. gateCommands' documented invariants (non-vacuous, never references plan.test_command, every unit command build-free, no package's unit suite twice) are asserted by real tests, and the final gate's sidecar I/O plus its BLOCKING branch — currently only the non-blocking scoped_out branch is covered — gain coverage. The state-invariants suite stops re-implementing findingCarryForwardKey and imports the production symbol.

Spec (do not restate it here): finalized_module_contracts["remediate-nextstep-and-final-gate"] — its inputs, outputs, 16 invariants, side_effects, validation_boundary, 9 failure_modes and seam_adjustments are the binding statement of what to build; the matching test specs in test_validator_plan (one per obligation) are the binding statement of how it is proven.

Invariants to make true: all 26 obligations listed in satisfies_obligations — the module contract obligation, 16 invariants (inv-1..inv-16) and 9 failure modes (fail-1..fail-9).

Write scope: src/remediate/steps/nextStep.ts, src/remediate/steps/finalGate.ts, src/remediate/steps/gateCommands.ts, tests/remediate/final-gate-extraction-equivalence.test.ts, tests/remediate/remediate-state-invariants.test.ts. Nothing outside it; a change another module owns is that module's node, not this one.

Coverage join (OBL-remediate-nextstep-and-final-gate-inv-16): this module owns the terminal disposition of exactly 9 approved finding id(s), derived mechanically from file_scope joined against approved-findings.json. Every owned id must reach a terminal disposition in .audit-tools/remediation-outcomes.json through dispositionToOutcomeStatus; the join is live-derived and must not be narrowed to make it pass.

Red-green law: every spec in test_validator_plan for these obligations is red-green validated — reintroduce the named defect, confirm the test goes RED, then restore by INVERTING the edit (never `git checkout --`). A test that stays green under its own NEGATIVE mutation does not close its obligation.

Verify with: npx vitest run tests/remediate/final-gate-extraction-equivalence.test.ts tests/remediate/next-step-lifecycle.test.ts tests/remediate/next-step-outcomes-contract.test.ts tests/remediate/next-step-pipeline-dispatch.test.ts tests/remediate/next-step-resume-gates.test.ts tests/remediate/next-step-review-gate.test.ts tests/remediate/remediate-state-invariants.test.ts, plus build/check/check:tests.

finding.title: Exclusion sign convention and zero-segment glob matching
finding.summary:
Defect classes closed: Scope and exclusion semantics that currently invert or under-match the user's stated intent. Exclusion clauses are treated as emphasis, so intent ordering boosts the very scope the user asked to ignore to the front of the queue — a sign convention that must be unit-tested directly against the documented contract. `**` in a glob never matches zero directory segments, so a root-level must_not_touch path silently falls out of protection: the matcher is fixed and tested on the idiomatic forms (root-level, zero-segment, escaped-regex) first. intentOrdering.ts is additionally an orphan with no tests and no production callers — its disposition (wire it or delete it) is decided here rather than left ambiguous.

finding.title: Content-derived charter delta identity
finding.summary:
Defect classes closed: Charter delta identity derived from position rather than content. delta_id collides when a subsystem mines two deltas on the same channel pair, and the collision propagates downstream into Finding.id and the clarification request_id, so two distinct deltas silently become one. Ids are derived from content so a repeated channel pair yields distinct, stable identities, and the partition layer that rebinds them is fixed on the same key space.

finding.title: Marker-gated route detection and availability-keyed edge cache
finding.summary:
Defect classes closed: Isolated logic defects in the deterministic extraction layer. Python route detection fabricates routes from @mock.patch and other non-route decorators, so extraction is gated on framework markers before any pattern-matching. finding.title: Exhaustive item-status partition and close-phase outcomes
finding.summary:
Defect classes closed: The remediation item-status partition and the close phase that consumes it. Gives `needs_clarification` a home in the status partitions so an unanswered item can neither land a green close nor lose its `original_state`, and rederives every partition from an exhaustive Record over the status union so a newly added status is a compile error instead of a silent permissive branch. Makes an unset `plan.test_command` a first-class never-ran outcome distinct from a passed suite (today it reports a passed verification trace and unlocks artifact deletion), stops the E2E-failure path transitioning to triage when there is nothing to re-block, records every close-phase early return in the durable structured run log instead of returning invisibly, and replaces the bare `endsWith` combined-failure attribution with a real path-key join so an innocent item is not blocked while the culprit resolves. Restructures close.ts so its suite imports it with typed imports rather than dynamic-import plus hand-written signature casts, which currently opts three describes out of the test-tree typecheck gate. Priority theme (T-002) — /design-check before the status-partition change.

finding.title: Atomic lock writes and classified heartbeat failures
finding.summary:
Defect classes closed: TOCTOU windows and swallowed evidence in the lock substrate itself (distinct from host-handoff-ingestion-substrate, which fixes a CALLER that failed to take a lock). Lock heartbeat failures are silently swallowed, so a loss of freshness is invisible — the failure cause is classified and recorded rather than caught and dropped. The suite lock's holder write is non-atomic, letting a reader delete a LIVE suite's registration; the write becomes temp-then-rename, and staleness decisions read a monotonic clock so a clock step cannot permit premature lock theft.

finding.title: Drift guards derive their expected set from source
finding.summary:
Defect classes closed: T-001 family one: guards that assert against a COPY, a source-text scan, or a self-selecting set, and therefore cannot detect the drift they claim to guard. The host-only-next-step seam test compares two hand-copied kind sets; the readPackageVersion regression test asserts on an inline re-implementation and never executes production code; the lens-drift guard only inspects enums that already contain "correctness", so a schema that DROPS a lens is never checked; the finding-ranks rank-table guard scans the retired packages/*/src layout and can never fail; and the retirement suite's catch-all optionalImport cannot distinguish a retired module from one that throws. finding.title: Archive-verify-then-delete report promotion

finding.title: Locked, path-contained host-handoff ingestion
finding.summary:
Defect classes closed: The loop-core host-handoff and result-ingestion boundary shared by both orchestrators, plus the submission-identity layer that defines the paths it enforces. resolveContainedPath (defined in submissionIdentity.ts, consumed by both hostHandoff.ts files) gets the path-containment refusal test it has none of. The audit-side accepted-results ledger stops being read-modify-written with no lock and is serialized through the shared LockedJsonStore. Dispatch-artifact validation stops being inert: today both discovery filters match zero files a live run produces — one scans a retired artifact name, the other a result filename no producer emits — so validation is rewritten to join on the filenames submissionIdentity actually mints, with a success-shaped empty scan reported as "no artifacts discovered", never as a pass. A remediation plan block with a missing dependency no longer silently bypasses dependency verification. Fixes shared logic ONCE in audit-tools/shared with per-mode policy rather than duplicating it across the two orchestrators. Loop-core substrate — commits touching it need a fresh staged-tree-bound review attestation.

finding.title: Exhaustive CI-red conclusion vocabulary and trigger paths
finding.summary:
Defect classes closed: The CI-red verdict and the trigger surface it reads. latestFailedWorkflows recognizes only the `failure` conclusion, so `timed_out`, `startup_failure`, and `action_required` all read as green to the closeout gate; the conclusion vocabulary becomes an exhaustive mapping in which a new or unrecognized conclusion is red (or a compile error), never silently green. The CI workflow's path filters are widened to the files verify:checks actually inspects — .claude/**, tsconfig.test.json, knip.json, eslint.config.js, .jscpd.json, .dependency-cruiser.cjs — so a change to a gate cannot skip the job that runs it. finding.title: Unbounded internal re-dispatch loop when an executor fails to satisfy its obligation state
finding.summary:
Inferred Contract: advanceAudit must gracefully halt the internal drain loop when an obligation execution does not transition its obligation state from missing/stale to satisfied.

Concrete Counterexample: An obligation (such as syntax_resolution) is marked "stale". runDrainStep invokes runSingleAdvanceStep, which dispatches syntax_resolution_executor. The executor runs and returns progress_made: true, but due to unparseable files or partial output, syntax_resolution remains "stale" in updated_bundle. Because nextStepIsDrainableRegen returns true and progress_made was true, runDrainStep yields { kind: "transition", state: updated_bundle }. The drain loop immediately re-evaluates and re-dispatches syntax_resolution_executor up to MAX_DRAIN_STEPS (64 times) in a single advanceAudit call before hitting the iteration cap.

Recommended Change: Track the sequence of selected obligations in DrainCtx in src/audit/orchestrator/advance.ts and halt the drain loop if the same obligation is selected consecutively without clearing its missing/stale state.

finding.title: Non-atomic multi-file writes in writeCoreArtifacts create torn artifact bundle states during concurrent reads
finding.summary:
Inferred Contract: Artifact bundle persistence (writeCoreArtifacts) must guarantee that concurrent readers (loadArtifactBundle) see a consistent, untorn snapshot of all inter-dependent phase artifacts.

entries.title: Non-monotonic Date.now() clock allows premature lock theft during system clock adjustments
entries.rationale: Disapproved by the user at the review gate (review-necessity: strategic).

finding.title: Non-monotonic Date.now() clock allows premature lock theft during system clock adjustments
finding.summary:
Inferred Contract: Lock staleness calculation (readStaleLockToken) must reliably distinguish abandoned locks from actively held locks regardless of system time adjustments.

Concrete Counterexample: A process acquires a file lock using acquireLock. The lock file mtimeMs is stamped with current system wall-clock time. During critical section execution, an NTP sync or system clock adjustment steps system wall-clock time backward by >30 seconds. In readStaleLockToken, now() evaluates to the shifted earlier time, causing now() - info.mtimeMs to evaluate incorrectly, or causing stale token checks in competing processes to classify live locks as stale. A competing process steals the lock via stealStaleLock while the original holder is still actively executing inside withFileLock.

Recommended Change: Use process.hrtime.bigint() or a monotonic clock source for relative duration and staleness checking in src/shared/io/fileLock.ts instead of wall-clock Date.now().

entries.title: Read-modify-write on the decisions ledger is unlocked, so concurrent answers lose each other
entries.rationale: Finding excluded by the intent checkpoint (filter or excluded scope).

finding.title: Read-modify-write on the decisions ledger is unlocked, so concurrent answers lose each other
finding.summary: Every mutation of the durable ledger is an unguarded read-modify-write: `recordDecision`, `recordReply`, and `recordCompletion` each call `readDecisions` and then `writeJson` over the full map with no lock, no compare-and-set, and no mtime check. Two overlapping invocations (two agent sessions in the same checkout, or the nightly routine writing while the owner answers) therefore lose whichever decision was written first — the later writer persists a map built from a pre-mutation snapshot. Because a settled subject is what stops a question being re-asked, a lost update silently resurrects an answered item, which is the exact failure mode the module's opening comment says it exists to end.
evidence: scripts/nightly/items.mjs:96-109 - `recordDecision` reads the full map, mutates one key, writes the full map, with nothing between the read and the write.
scripts/nightly/items.mjs:129-133 - `recordReply` performs the same unguarded read-modify-write.
scripts/nightly/items.mjs:147-155 - `recordCompletion` performs the same unguarded read-modify-write.
scripts/nightly/items.mjs:18-21 - the module imports only `node:child_process`, `node:crypto`, `node:fs`, and `node:path`; no locking primitive is imported or used.
scripts/nightly/items.mjs:8-10 - the header states an answered-and-still-asked item is what 'trains the owner to ignore the channel', which is the consequence of a lost update here.
scripts/nightly/answer.mjs:46-48 - the CLI snapshots `readDecisions(ROOT)` at startup and `recordDecision` re-reads later, so a single run already spans two independent reads of the same file.
reproduction: Start two `node scripts/nightly/answer.mjs <ID_A|ID_B> "..."` runs against the same checkout so their reads interleave before either write.
Inspect .claude/nightly-decisions.json: only one of the two new subject keys is present.
The lost subject is re-raised as unanswered on the next nightly run.

finding.title: Three gates take their scan root from process.cwd() with no repo anchor, so an invocation from a subdirectory silently narrows the scan and still reports success
finding.summary: check-control-bytes.mjs, check-memory-citations.mjs and check-version-gates.mjs derive their scope from the process working directory instead of anchoring on the repo. check-control-bytes spawns `git ls-files` with no `cwd` option and then `readFileSync(file)` on the returned repo-relative paths; check-memory-citations does the same and additionally derives the memory store slug from `resolve(process.cwd())`; check-version-gates defaults `collectSources(root = process.cwd())`. Their peers in the same directory do anchor: check-doc-manifest.mjs, check-guard-reach.mjs, check-backlog-budget.mjs and check-backlog-status-tokens.mjs all compute repoRoot from `import.meta.url`, and attest-constitutional-doc-change.mjs / check-nightly-routine-prompt.mjs / check-philosophy-brief.mjs honour `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`. A gate whose reach depends on the caller's cwd is the false-green shape the repo's guard-reach doctrine exists to remove.

finding.title: Result corroboration inspects only the tip commit, so a multi-commit landing escapes allowed_files and run-start-dirty enforcement
finding.summary: CONFIRMED AT HEAD, stands at high/high with no narrowing. corroborateHostResult only requires baseline_commit to be an ANCESTOR of commit_evidence.after, then derives the changed-file set from a single-commit `git diff-tree` on the tip. Files touched by any intermediate commit between baseline and tip are never compared against workItem.allowed_files nor against state.run_start_dirty, so out-of-scope edits land accepted. Scope is exactly one function pair (corroborateHostResult + gitChangedFilesOfCommit); the fix is to diff the baseline..landed range instead of the tip's own diff.

"-r",
          "-z",
          commit,
if (!gitCommitIsAncestor(root, baseline, landed))
const actualFiles = gitChangedFilesOfCommit(root, landed)
acceptedFiles = corroborated.changedFiles;
nextState.applied_edit_surface = [...landedFiles].sort(compareCodeUnits);

evidence: hostHandoff.ts:992 `if (!gitCommitIsAncestor(root, baseline, landed))` — ancestry only; the tip is never required to be a direct child of the baseline.

hostHandoff.ts:931-952 `gitChangedFilesOfCommit` runs `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r -z <commit>` against the single landed commit, i.e. the tip-vs-its-parent diff, not `baseline..landed`.
hostHandoff.ts:1015-1021 and 1025-1034 both consume that single-commit `actualFiles` for the allowed_files and run_start_dirty checks.

src/remediate/steps/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts:992 - `if (!gitCommitIsAncestor(root, baseline, landed))` is an ancestry test only; the tip is never required to be a direct child of the baseline, so arbitrarily many commits may sit between them.

src/remediate/steps/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts:931-952 - `gitChangedFilesOfCommit` runs `git diff-tree --root --no-commit-id --name-only -r -z <commit>` against the single landed commit, i.e. tip-vs-parent, not the `baseline..landed` range.
src/remediate/steps/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts:1006-1007 - `const actualFiles = gitChangedFilesOfCommit(root, landed)` is the sole mechanically derived file set used for the rest of corroboration.
src/remediate/steps/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts:1015-1021 - the allowed_files containment check consumes that same single-commit `actualFiles`.
src/remediate/steps/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts:1025-1034 - the run_start_dirty overlap check also consumes only that single-commit `actualFiles`.

src/remediate/steps/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts:1326 - `acceptedFiles = corroborated.changedFiles` feeds the persisted applied_edit_surface (line 1337), so the intermediate commits are invisible downstream too.
The ancestry check (line 992) only requires baseline to be an ancestor of landed, allowing multiple commits between them.
The gitChangedFilesOfCommit function (lines 945-947) shows that only the landed commit is used to compute changed files, ignoring any intermediate commits.
The changed files from the tip (line 1006) are checked against allowed_files (lines 1015-1017) and run_start_dirty (not shown here but similar).
The accepted files from corroboration (line 1327) are used to update the applied_edit_surface (line 1342), so intermediate commits are not recorded in the state.

finding.title: buildRequeueTargets cannot report a never-classified file, so an unaudited file disappears from the coverage gap list
finding.summary: createCoverageMatrix initialises every file with `required_lenses: []` and `audit_status: 'pending'`; only applyUnitCoverage populates required_lenses. buildRequeueTargets computes `missing_lenses = required_lenses \ completed_lenses` and then drops every entry with an empty missing_lenses list. A file that was never matched to any unit therefore has required_lenses [] → missing_lenses [] → it is filtered out entirely, and applyFileCoverage never moves it off 'pending' either. The requeue list — the mechanism that is supposed to prove coverage — reports 'nothing missing' for exactly the files that received zero audit attention, so an unclassified file is indistinguishable from a fully covered one.

src/audit/coverage.ts:94-102 `.filter((file) => file.audit_status !== 'excluded')` … `.filter((item) => item.missing_lenses.length > 0)` — the only exclusion tested is 'excluded'; an unclassified file passes the first filter and is removed by the second.
src/audit/coverage.ts:77-87 applyFileCoverage only promotes to 'complete'/'partial'; a file with no required and no completed lenses stays 'pending' and is never surfaced.

entries.title: CP-CORR-001 STANDS: split cycle tiers become a phase barrier that orders one cycle member behind the other at dispatch
entries.rationale: Finding excluded by the intent checkpoint (filter or excluded scope).

finding.title: CP-CORR-001 STANDS: split cycle tiers become a phase barrier that orders one cycle member behind the other at dispatch
finding.summary: Deepening verdict on CP-CORR-001: the defect is confirmed at its source and its consumption site, so the finding STANDS at severity medium / confidence high (not high/high). Source confirmed: derivePhaseCut's memoized DFS returns 0 on the back-edge without settling the node, so for A->B->A the sorted traversal settles B at tier 1 and A at tier 2 — the documented 'members are placed together at one tier' contract is not met, and no tier 0 exists at all in that run (phases become consumers-1 + integration, no foundations). Consumption confirmed in the assigned file: promoteImplementationDagToExtractedPlan re-keys phase_cut.module_phase by moduleSlug and stamps block.phase_ordinal whenever the cut has more than one phase, and dispatch reads that ordinal as a hard barrier (a block may not dispatch until EVERY lower-phase block is verified-complete). So the two members of a genuine mutual dependency are gated one behind the other rather than authored together. Scope should NARROW in one respect: the split is only observable when the cut is multi-phase (hasMultiPhase), and it does not deadlock — the earlier member is still dispatchable — so the impact is a wrong (and design-hostile) serialization plus a misleading critique prompt, not a stuck run. The prompt text the critic sees also asserts the members were tiered together, which is false for the same input.

src/remediate/contractPipeline/phaseCut.ts:97 - `const t = maxDep + 1; tier.set(name, t);` — each member still gains a tier on the unwind, so A->B->A settles B=1 and A=2 (traced by hand through the sorted `for (const name of [...names].sort()) computeTier(name)` at line 102)

src/remediate/contractPipeline/phaseCut.ts:372 - renderPhaseCutSection tells the critic 'its members were tiered together', so the critique prompt asserts a property the cut does not have
src/remediate/steps/contractPipeline.ts:3083 - `const hasMultiPhase = phaseCut ? phaseCut.phases.length > 1 : false;` — the split cycle produces two phases, so ordinals ARE stamped
src/remediate/steps/contractPipeline.ts:3283 - `const phaseOrdinal = hasMultiPhase ? phaseOrdinalForObligations(...)` and line 3303 spreads `phase_ordinal` onto the promoted block

src/remediate/steps/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts:424 - `const phaseBarrierClear = (phase) => lowerPhaseBlocks(phase).every(isVerifiedNow);` — the stamped ordinal is a hard dispatch barrier, so the later cycle member waits on the earlier one

src/remediate/steps/contractPipeline.ts:2903 - `const cut = await ensurePhaseCutArtifact(artifactsDir);` at the critique phase, and line 2906 renders it — the same split cut is both shown to the critic and persisted for promotion

finding.title: merge-results double-counts a task in `total`, so the accepted/rejected summary is arithmetically wrong
finding.summary: `failing` is keyed by nothing and accumulates per-result entries during the file scan, while the manifest loop separately appends one entry per unsatisfied task. `total = passing.length + failing.length` therefore exceeds the number of assigned tasks whenever a result file is a duplicate, unknown, or unparsable, and the same task can be counted both accepted and rejected. Example: task A has a valid result plus a second copy in another file — the duplicate copy pushes a `failing` entry for A, the valid copy pushes A into `passing`, and the run prints `1/2 tasks valid` for a one-task manifest while exiting non-zero.
evidence: dispatch/merge-results.mjs:86-94 pushes a `failing` entry for a duplicate result while the first copy is still eligible for `passing`.
dispatch/merge-results.mjs:144 `const total = passing.length + failing.length;` treats the two arrays as a partition of the manifest, which they are not.
dispatch/merge-results.mjs:152-161 reports `total`/`accepted`/`rejected` in both the JSON summary line and the human line.

entries.title: A spawn failure on the first resolved candidate aborts the fallback chain
entries.rationale: Finding excluded by the intent checkpoint (filter or excluded scope).

finding.title: A spawn failure on the first resolved candidate aborts the fallback chain
finding.summary: runFirstAvailableCommand returns unconditionally after the first candidate that resolves, even when spawnSync never executed anything (result.error set, result.status null). A candidate whose binary resolves on PATH but fails to exec (ENOENT on a dangling shim, EACCES on a non-executable file, EPERM, ENOBUFS) therefore masks every remaining candidate, and the function reports exitCode null with empty stdout/stderr rather than trying the next available command. The name and contract of the function is 'first available command', but a failed exec is not availability.
evidence: Lines 120-126: `const result = spawnSync(...)` — the return value's `error` field is never inspected before returning.
Lines 128-140: the `return` is inside the `for (const candidate of candidates)` body and unconditional, so the loop can never reach a second candidate once one resolves.
Lines 137-139: `error: result.error ? new Error(...)` — the code demonstrably anticipates spawn failure yet still consumes the candidate as the answer.
runtime:unit:src-audit: not_confirmed — Deterministic runtime command failed with exit code 1: npm test
reproduction: Pass two candidates where the first resolves via resolveFromPath to a path that exists but is not executable (e.g. a directory or a non-exec file) and the second is a valid command.
Observe runFirstAvailableCommand returns the first candidate with exitCode null and a populated `error`, never attempting the second.

Combined with the unconditional return in runFirstAvailableCommand, this converts a benign name collision into a hard failure of the whole candidate chain instead of a skip.

Lines 72-75: `const candidatePath = join(dir, `${command}${ext}`); if (existsSync(candidatePath)) return candidatePath;` — the win32 bare-name probe (ext === "") makes a directory hit especially likely.

Lines 98-104: `const repoLocalPath = join(root, candidate.command); if (existsSync(repoLocalPath))` — same test against the repo root, where directories named like tools are common (e.g. `scripts`, `node_modules/.bin` siblings).

finding.title: spawnSync runs with the default maxBuffer, silently truncating large analyzer output
finding.summary: The spawnSync options set cwd, env, encoding, windowsHide and stdio but not maxBuffer, so Node's 1 MiB default applies. When a local tool emits more than 1 MiB on a stream (routine for JSON reporters such as lint/dead-code/dependency analyzers on a large repo), Node kills the child, sets result.error to ENOBUFS and returns TRUNCATED stdout. The returned LocalCommandResult still carries a plausible exitCode and a partial stdout, so a caller that parses stdout sees a malformed or partial payload rather than a clear failure.

Lines 134-136: `exitCode: result.status, stdout: result.stdout ?? ""` — the truncated stdout is returned alongside the status with no indication that the stream was cut.

reproduction: Invoke runFirstAvailableCommand with a candidate whose child writes >1 MiB to stdout.

finding.title: Analyzer source-size guards compare UTF-16 code units against a byte budget
finding.summary: The css, html and python tree-sitter analyzers each guard with `if (content.length > MAX_*_SOURCE_BYTES) continue;` where the constant is `512 * 1024` and named ...SOURCE_BYTES, but `content` is a decoded UTF-8 string, so `.length` counts UTF-16 code units, not bytes. The mismatch is silent and platform-independent, and the divergence grows with exactly the inputs the guard exists to protect against.

finding.summary: The module registers cleanup with `process.on("exit", ...)`, which does not fire for SIGINT/SIGTERM (the normal way a hung smoke is stopped) or for an abrupt kill. Each such run leaves a `audit-tools-smoke-state-*` directory behind in the OS temp root, and the same temp root is where the pack cache and the vitest suite-lock holders live, so the accumulation is unbounded across CI/dev laps. The comment names the OS temp dir as the backstop, but no OS reclaims per-run temp dirs during a session; the honest fix is signal handlers alongside the exit hook.
evidence: scripts/shared/hermetic-state-dir.mjs:15 `process.on("exit", () => { ... rmSync(stateDir, ...) })` is the only cleanup registration.

finding.title: Passthrough drift guard asserts only a negative, so it passes vacuously if the wrapper never dispatches
finding.summary: The `status` passthrough test (lines 186-204) ignores the child's exit code and asserts only `expect(stderrRef.value).not.toMatch(/Unknown command: status/)`. Any failure mode that produces no output at all — wrapper crash before dispatch, missing dist, spawn-level error surfacing a different message, or an empty stderr — satisfies the assertion. The test therefore cannot distinguish 'the passthrough reached the dist CLI' from 'the wrapper died first', which is exactly the regression class its comment claims to guard (wrapper/CLI parity being structural). A positive assertion is needed: that the dist CLI's own `status` output or its authoritative error text appears, mirroring the sibling `cleanup` test at lines 206-227 which does assert positive stdout markers.

finding.title: PATH resolution accepts any binary of the right name, silently defeating the pinned-version invariant
finding.summary: `resolveBinary` probes `spec.versionProbeArgs` and, on exit 0, returns `command: spec.binaryName` without ever comparing the probe's output to `spec.version`. The stated invariant is "version is PINNED (reproducibility)", and the candidates encode exact versions (gitleaks 8.21.2, osv-scanner 2.4.0, hadolint 2.14.0, actionlint 1.7.12), yet an arbitrarily old or new on-PATH build is used in preference to the pinned one. Analyzer output then varies by machine while the artifact records the pinned version, so leads are not reproducible and rule-id/severity drift across hosts is invisible. The probe also runs in `process.cwd()` rather than the repo root, so the resolution is sensitive to the caller's working directory.
evidence: src/shared/analyzers/binaryAcquisition.ts:128-132 — `const probe = run(spec.versionProbeArgs, process.cwd()); if (!probe.error && probe.status === 0) { return { status: "path", command: spec.binaryName }; }` — `probe.stdout` is never inspected and `spec.version` is never used on this branch.
src/shared/analyzers/candidates.ts:66-73, 563-571, 736-746, 832-841 — every BinarySpec declares a concrete pinned `version` and `safetyProfile.version_pinning: "pinned"`.

reproduction: Install gitleaks 8.0.0 on PATH, then call `resolveBinary(GITLEAKS_BINARY)` — it returns `{status:"path", command:"gitleaks"}` even though the spec pins 8.21.2.

finding.title: The verify:checks step parser treats every whitespace token after the profile-run label as a gate step
finding.summary: `verifyChecksSteps()` slices package.json's `verify:checks` at the literal `verify-checks` marker and splits the remainder on whitespace with no validation that a token names a package script. Today the script is exactly `node scripts/shared/profile-run.mjs verify-checks <step>…`, so it works; the moment anything is appended (`&& npm run x`, a `--flag`, a path argument) those tokens become 'steps'. finding.title: A signal-killed anchor command is scored 'refuted', quarantining a finding on evidence that the run never produced
finding.summary: evaluateExpectation treats `exitCode === null` — the shape a process killed by a signal reports (OOM, SIGSEGV, external kill) — as a normal verdict input. For `exit_zero` it yields `confirmed: false`, and verifyFindingAnchor maps a non-confirmed verdict straight to `refuted`, which combineGroundingWithAnchor turns into a quarantined-EXCLUDED finding. Only the explicit `timed_out` path is routed to `inconclusive`; every other abnormal termination is indistinguishable from a genuine refutation, so a real finding can be silently dropped because the checker died rather than because the claim is false. The module's own contract says a refuting run must be a run that DISPROVED the claim.

finding.title: `mergeGitignoreBlock` loses user lines / duplicates the block when only one marker survives
finding.summary: src/shared/io/gitignoreArtifacts.ts:181-199 only takes the in-place replacement branch when BOTH markers are found and ordered (`beginIdx !== -1 && endIdx !== -1 && endIdx > beginIdx`). A half-present managed block (a user or tool truncation that leaves only the BEGIN or only the END marker) silently falls through to the append branch instead of being repaired: (a) an orphaned END marker with no BEGIN causes the new block to be appended, and on the NEXT run `beginIdx` (the fresh block, late in the file) is greater than `endIdx` (the orphan, early), so the ordering guard fails again and another full block is appended — the function is no longer idempotent and managed blocks accumulate without bound; (b) an orphaned BEGIN marker with no END likewise appends, and on the next run `beginIdx` is the orphan and `endIdx` is the new block's end, so `before = slice(0, orphanBegin)` and `after = ''` — every user line written between the orphan BEGIN and the appended block is DELETED from the user's .gitignore. The function is the sole writer of a file the consuming repo owns, and its own docstring promises 'user lines outside the markers are never touched'.

finding.summary: renderCharterDeltaPrompt guards the register itself (`register?.`) but then dereferences `.ceiling.rung` without a guard. The register is loaded from disk and the only load-time check is a schema_version equality test (discard-on-mismatch), not a structural validation — so a v2-stamped register whose `ceiling` is missing (truncated/partial write, hand edit, an out-of-band writer) raises `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` while rendering the host prompt, instead of degrading to the safe non-deepest branch. The prior finding STANDS at low/low: the failure path is real but narrow, the type declares `ceiling` required, and every in-repo writer sets it.
evidence: src/audit/cli/charterDeltaPrompt.ts:20 - `const register = bundle.charter_register;` reads an OPTIONAL bundle field (ArtifactBundle is `Partial<ArtifactPayloadMap> & {...}` at src/audit/io/artifacts.ts:148), so the author knew absence was possible.

src/audit/cli/charterDeltaPrompt.ts:22 - `const deepest = register?.ceiling.rung === "deepest";` — optional chaining stops after `register`; `.ceiling` and `.rung` are unguarded, so a present-but-incomplete register throws rather than falling to the non-deepest branch.

src/audit/io/artifacts.ts:374 - load applies only `discardOnSchemaVersionMismatch(bundle.charter_register, CHARTER_REGISTER_SCHEMA_VERSION)`; a register whose `schema_version` matches passes through with no field-level validation of `ceiling`.
src/audit/types/charterRegister.ts:51 - `ceiling: Ceiling;` is a required TYPE field only; it constrains in-repo writers, not JSON already on disk.

src/audit/cli/charterDeltaPrompt.ts:80-96 - the value only selects between two prompt text blocks (True-nomination authorization vs. its refusal), so the blast radius of a wrong/absent value is a prompt-text branch, not a routing or gate decision.

src/audit/orchestrator/charterDeltaExecutor.ts:95 - `allowTrueNominations: register.ceiling.rung === "deepest"` is the ENFORCEMENT half and reads the same field equally unguarded, confirming the prompt-side access is not the security boundary; the prompt is advisory text only.

finding.title: Auditor-contract fixture hardcodes summary counts that can silently desync from its own findings/work_blocks arrays
finding.summary: In generate-auditor-contract-fixture.mjs the emitted model's summary block is written as literals (finding_count: 3, work_block_count: 2, severity_breakdown {high:1, medium:1, low:1}, audited_file_count: 3) while findings and work_blocks are real arrays defined above. finding.title: Scope dedup silently prefers file-derived tasks over flow-derived tasks
finding.summary: buildRequeuePayload merges as [...fileTasks, ...flowTasks] and then runs dedupeByScope, which is first-wins on the `lens:file_paths` signature (line 28-33). Whenever a flow requeue task covers exactly the same lens and file set as a file requeue task, the flow task is the one dropped, purely because of concatenation order. Any flow-specific identity or metadata carried on the flow task (e.g. its flow unit/task id and rationale) is lost, and the surviving task is attributed to the file source. The preference is implicit in argument order rather than expressed as a policy, so a later reordering of the spread would silently invert which task survives.
evidence: src/audit/orchestrator/requeueCommand.ts:28 — signature = `${task.lens}:${[...task.file_paths].sort().join(",")}`; first occurrence wins.
src/audit/orchestrator/requeueCommand.ts:63 — dedupeByScope(dedupeTasks([...fileTasks, ...flowTasks])) fixes precedence by spread order only.

finding.title: Auto-fix formatters are invoked with every in-scope file path on one command line, which exceeds the OS argument limit on any medium-or-larger repo
finding.summary: runAutoFixExecutor (src/audit/orchestrator/autoFixExecutor.ts:143-199) expands pathsForExtensions() straight into the spawn arguments: `['--write', ...prettierPaths]`, `[...pythonPaths]`, `['fix','--force',...sqlPaths]`, `['-w',...goPaths]`. There is no chunking and no cap on the path count. Windows caps a command line at ~32k characters (and .cmd shim invocations lower still — this repo routes package-manager shims through the command shell), and POSIX caps at ARG_MAX. A repo with a few thousand in-scope TypeScript files therefore produces a spawn that fails wholesale; runFormatter classifies the failure as `failed` (line 78) and the run records `Formatters failed: prettier` with no indication that the cause was argument length, so no file gets formatted and the failure mode looks like a missing tool. The fix is deterministic batching of the path list under a conservative per-invocation length budget.
evidence: src/audit/orchestrator/autoFixExecutor.ts:164 `{ command: "prettier", args: ["--write", ...prettierPaths], display }` — the whole in-scope path list becomes argv.
src/audit/orchestrator/autoFixExecutor.ts:115-126 `pathsForExtensions` returns an unbounded sorted array; no caller chunks it.
src/audit/orchestrator/autoFixExecutor.ts:78-88 a failed spawn is only recorded as `failed_tools`, losing the cause.
runtime:unit:src-audit: not_confirmed — Deterministic runtime command failed with exit code 1: npm test
reproduction: Run the auto-fix executor against a repo with several thousand in-scope .ts files on Windows.
Observe the prettier spawn fails and `auto_fixes_applied.json` reports failed_tools:['prettier'] with zero files formatted.

finding.title: black / sqlfluff / gofmt are run unconditionally over in-scope files while prettier is gated on a detected config
finding.summary: In runAutoFixExecutor (src/audit/orchestrator/autoFixExecutor.ts:155-199) prettier only runs when hasPrettierConfig(root) confirms the audited repo actually opted into prettier (line 155). The Python, SQL and Go formatters have no equivalent gate: the presence of a single in-scope `.py`, `.sql` or `.go` file is enough to run `black`, `sqlfluff fix --force` (which rewrites files in place and, with --force, applies fixes the linter is unsure about) and `gofmt -w` across the audited tree. An auditing tool rewriting the audited repository's source with a formatter the project never configured is an unrequested mutation: it produces a large spurious diff, can conflict with the project's real formatter, and for sqlfluff --force can change SQL semantics-adjacent formatting under a guessed dialect. The asymmetry with the prettier branch shows the config gate is the intended contract.

finding.title: An unreadable or malformed repo manifest silently makes every recovery refuse
finding.summary: repoFileUniverse swallows ALL failures of readOptionalJsonFile with .catch(() => undefined) and also treats a manifest whose `files` array is absent as an empty set. finding.title: Task-affinity canonicalization silently swaps from/to, discarding direction and hiding duplicate reversed edges
finding.summary: `canonicalizeTaskAffinityGraph` rewrites every edge into lexicographic `from < to` order regardless of `kind`. Since the canonicalizer is applied at the artifact persistence seam (`canonicalizeAffinityArtifactValue` for `task_affinity_graph.json`), any edge whose `kind` carries a direction is silently reversed on write — the persisted artifact then asserts a relationship the producer did not. The same rewrite also makes two genuinely distinct edges (`a→b` and `b→a`, same kind) collapse to identical content while both are retained, so the artifact keeps a duplicate pair whose only prior distinction was the direction that was just erased. There is no dedupe after the swap and no guard that `kind` is symmetric.

src/shared/affinityArtifacts.ts:194-207 — the canonicalizer is applied to the persisted `task_affinity_graph.json` value, so the rewrite is what lands on disk.

entries.title: check-memory-citations' citation regex spans newlines, so a line-final `memory: <name>` citation is silently skipped instead of validated
entries.rationale: Finding excluded by the intent checkpoint (filter or excluded scope).

finding.title: check-memory-citations' citation regex spans newlines, so a line-final `memory: <name>` citation is silently skipped instead of validated
finding.summary: The citation pattern is `/memory:\s*([^)*]+)/g` (line 60) and is run against the WHOLE file text with `text.matchAll`. The negated class `[^)*]` includes `\n`, so a citation that is not closed by `)` or `*` on its own line keeps consuming subsequent lines until the next `)` or `*` anywhere in the document. The captured run is then split on `,` and each segment is filtered by `/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/` — a segment that has swallowed a newline plus following prose fails that test and is dropped. Net effect: the cited name is never checked against the memory store, so a dangling citation in that (very ordinary) form passes the gate green. The gate's whole purpose is that a citation to a deleted note re-asserts a refuted design; a silently unchecked citation is the exact failure it exists to stop.
evidence: scripts/check-memory-citations.mjs:60 `const CITATION = /memory:\s*([^)*]+)/g;`
scripts/check-memory-citations.mjs:76 `for (const match of text.matchAll(CITATION))` — matched against whole-file text, not per line.
scripts/check-memory-citations.mjs:80 `.filter((n) => /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/.test(n))` — a multi-line capture segment fails this and is discarded silently.
runtime:unit:scripts: not_confirmed — Deterministic runtime command failed with exit code 1: npm test
reproduction: Add a tracked markdown line ending exactly `see memory: no-such-note-at-all` with no closing `)` or `*` on that line, followed by ordinary prose lines.
Run `node scripts/check-memory-citations.mjs` with the memory store present.
The gate reports success: the capture ran past the line end and the concatenated segment failed the slug filter, so the dangling name was never compared to the store.

entries.rationale: Finding excluded by the intent checkpoint (filter or excluded scope).

finding.title: appendResultsToLedger seeds its dedupe set only from records that already carry an idempotency_key, so a legacy ledger admits duplicates
finding.summary: ledger.ts:173-189 builds `seen` by reading `record.idempotency_key` off each EXISTING record and skipping any non-string, but it never runs those records through `stampLedgerKeys`. A pre-O2 (or externally hand-repaired) ledger whose records lack `idempotency_key` therefore contributes nothing to `seen`, and re-ingesting the same logical result appends a second record — breaking INV-2 (idempotent on idempotency_key), the invariant the module's own header claims holds "by construction (never by a caller remembering them)". The read path already handles this case (`selectCurrentResults` at ledger.ts:110 stamps on read, and the doc-comment says "a pre-O2 ledger still resolves"); the append path does not, so the two halves disagree. The duplicate then survives into synthesis unless it happens to lose the `attemptOf` comparison — and two base records tie at attempt 0, where `>` keeps the FIRST, so the newer findings are the ones discarded.

finding.title: partitionFromGroups picks the community representative from UN-normalized group members while keying on normalized paths
finding.summary: partitionFromGroups sorts the raw group members to choose `rep`, then normalizes each member with toPosix before `partition.set(m, rep)`. The representative — the community LABEL every member of the group is keyed to — therefore keeps whatever separator form the caller supplied, while membership lookup uses the posix form. Two consequences: the same logical group supplied with backslash paths yields a different community id than the posix form (so partitions built from differently-normalized sources never agree, diluting the agreement mean in decompose), and the sort that selects the representative orders on the raw strings, so the choice of representative itself is separator-dependent. Every other path in this module funnels through toPosix (weightedGraph line 39-40, buildStructureSources line 131), so this is the one unnormalized seam.

src/audit/decompose/sources.ts:87-89 `const m = toPosix(member); if (partition.has(m)) partition.set(m, rep);` — members normalized, label not.

finding.title: Derived-file preflight converts a 60s timeout or a slow npm script into an attestation refusal indistinguishable from a real staleness failure
finding.summary: runDerivedFilePreflight runs each triggered check with `execSync(..., { timeout: 60_000 })` and pushes ANY thrown error into `failures`, whose non-emptiness makes the caller refuse to bind an attestation. A timeout (ETIMEDOUT / SIGTERM kill) and a shell/npm resolution error are therefore reported with the same shape and the same `fix` line as a genuinely stale derived file, so the operator is told to regenerate a file that is already current. Given the module's own stated purpose — never make a repo un-attestable for reasons other than real staleness, with unwired scripts explicitly failing open — an environment-caused kill silently landing in the fail-closed bucket is an inconsistency in the failure taxonomy, not a deliberate policy.

finding.title: A null baseline hallucination_rate is rendered as "0.0%" instead of "n/a" in both gate messages
finding.summary: fmt() exists precisely to render a null rate as "n/a", but both call sites that print the baseline value apply `?? 0` first (`fmt(baseline?.hallucination_rate ?? 0)` and `fmt(baseline.hallucination_rate ?? 0)`), so the null is consumed before fmt can see it and the operator is told the baseline hallucination rate was 0.0%. finding.title: readRequiredSource resets process.exitCode to 0, erasing a failure already recorded by an earlier postinstall step
finding.summary: readRequiredSource sets `process.exitCode = 0` when a source file is missing, to express 'skip, not failure'. But process.exitCode is process-global state that finishPostinstall also owns (`if (counts.failed > 0) process.exitCode = 1`). Any postinstall that installs one asset group, records a failure, and only then reaches a missing optional/required source for the next group has its non-zero exit silently reset to success. The correct expression of 'this is a skip' is to not touch the exit code at all; writing 0 is an unconditional clobber of a signal this module does not own.

finding.title: detectCyclicSeamObligations reports every node downstream of a cycle as a cycle member
finding.summary: Cycle membership is taken to be every node left with in-degree > 0 after Kahn's drain. A node that merely DEPENDS (transitively) on a cycle also never reaches in-degree 0, so it is collected into cycleNodes and then union-found into the same component as the real cycle. The reported DetectedCycle.members therefore over-reports: acyclic consumers are named as cycle participants, and validateCycleBreak rewrites THEIR needs edges to the mediator (cycleSet drives the patch), altering a graph region that was never cyclic. A self-loop (a node listing itself in needs) is likewise reported as a one-member cycle despite the documented 'N >= 2 nodes'.

src/remediate/contractPipeline/cyclicSeamResolution.ts:125 - the union-find pass then joins those descendants into the same component via their needs edges

finding.title: sortNodeInputs breaks ties on files[0] BEFORE the file list is normalized, so node order depends on host input order
finding.summary: assembleCharters documents that the same nodes plus the same hint and universe always yield the same units, ids, and charter selection (lines 317-320 docblock). But the ordering pass runs first: sortNodeInputs breaks its final tie on `a.files[0]` (line 275) while the files array is still exactly as the host submitted it — deduplication and sorting of `files` only happen afterwards, during grounding (line 336). finding.title: The residual unit id "provably collision-free" claim rests on an assumption the hint contract does not make
finding.summary: The join docblock states residual unit ids cannot collide with hint ids because "a residual scope contains no hint member, so its first file can never equal a hint id, which IS a hint member" (lines 310-313). The hint is a `node_id -> members` map (line 292) built from the decomposition consensus (src/audit/orchestrator/charterExtractionExecutor.ts:41-47); nothing requires a consensus node_id to appear inside its own members list, so the final step of that argument is not guaranteed by any contract. If a consensus node_id happens to be a path string that is not one of its own members, a residual unit whose lexicographically-first file equals it produces two drafts with the same node_id, and `byNode` in assembleDeltas (line 519) keeps only the last, silently routing every delta for one unit onto the other. No code enforces the assumed property, so this is a claimed proof that could go stale rather than a currently-demonstrated defect.

finding.title: A `halt` entry in triage_resolution.json returns to closing while earlier entries have already mutated item state
finding.summary: runTriagePhase iterates resolution.items in array order (triage.ts:230-267). `retry` entries mutate the live item objects in place (retryBlockedItem sets status='pending', bumps rework_count) and `ignore` entries set status='ignored'. When a LATER entry carries action='halt', the function returns `{...state, status: 'closing'}` at lines 239-246 — a shallow spread, so all preceding mutations persist. The retried items are left in the non-terminal `pending` status inside a closing run (force-closed to `abandoned` by close), archiveImplementResultsForRetries is never called for them so their stale host result files stay on disk, and triage-outcome.json records them as 'retried' in a run that halted. The outcome therefore depends on the ORDER of entries in the host-written resolution: halt-first yields a clean halt, halt-last yields a half-applied one.

entries.title: addTaskBlock silently drops a whole chunk of files when its derived task id was already seen
entries.rationale: Finding excluded by the intent checkpoint (filter or excluded scope).

finding.title: addTaskBlock silently drops a whole chunk of files when its derived task id was already seen
finding.summary: The finding STANDS at HEAD and its confidence is raised from low to high, because the reachability gap that justified the low rating is now closed by a concrete upstream producer. Both loops in addTaskBlock are guarded by the `seen` set with no else branch, so a colliding task id discards the chunk's file paths with no task, no diagnostic, and no coverage bookkeeping. The remainder path cannot collide (buildRemainderBlocks groups on `${lens}|${unitId}` and addTaskBlock is called with scopeId = block.unitId, so each lens/unit pair reaches the function once), but the FLOW path can: flow scopeId is `flow:${block.flow_id}`, and flow ids are not unique. buildCriticalFlowManifest mints ids by regex-sanitizing a surface id or a file path (`id: \`flow:data:${path.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9:_-]/g, "-")}\``), which maps both `/` and `.` to `-`, so `src/foo/bar.ts` and `src/foo-bar.ts` produce the identical id; dedupeFlows keys on name|paths|concerns and NOT on id, so both survive as distinct flows sharing one id. claimFlowReviewBlocks then emits two blocks with the same flow_id and lens but disjoint file_paths (the `assigned` set only suppresses the second block when its paths overlap the first), and the second block's files are dropped in addTaskBlock. Those paths keep an unsatisfied required lens in the coverage matrix, so coverage can never reach completion and the cause is invisible. Scope narrows to the flow-block call site (line 366-383) as the reachable trigger, but the defective shape is in both loops of addTaskBlock and the correct fix is still there — merge or disambiguate on collision instead of discarding — with flow-id uniqueness worth enforcing upstream as defense in depth.

finding.title: Comment scanner applies JS string-literal skipping to markup/hash/CSS/SQL syntaxes, so a bare apostrophe swallows the rest of the file's comments
finding.summary: scanCommentSpans unconditionally treats `"`, `'` and backtick as string-literal openers (commentDecomposition.ts:109-130) regardless of the file's CommentSyntax. For MARKUP (.html/.md/.vue/.svelte), CSS, HASH_ONLY (.yaml/.sh/.toml) and SQL_LIKE files, an apostrophe in ordinary prose or an unmatched quote is not a string delimiter — the scanner enters string mode and consumes forward to the next matching quote, or to EOF when there is none. Every comment span between those two points is lost. Because extractCommentText and stripCommentText are both thin consumers of this scanner (documented at :90-95), the loss is symmetric: deriveCommentDecomposition silently misses the intent-declared coupling edges from those files (no error, just a smaller edge set), and stripCommentText leaves the comment text in the 'comment-blind' view.

finding.title: tsc diagnostic parser cannot match Windows drive-letter paths
finding.summary: runTsc parses tsc output with /^([^:]+)\((\d+),\d+\):\s+(error\s+TS\d+:.*)$/. The leading group excludes ':', so any diagnostic emitted with an absolute Windows path (e.g. 'C:\\repo\\src\\a.ts(3,5): error TS2322: ...') never matches. Every such diagnostic is dropped, results stays empty, and the executor then reports status 'parse_error' instead of the real type errors — on a project whose stated invariant is OS-agnostic behaviour.

finding.summary: The prior finding's mechanism is confirmed — `^([^:]+)\(` cannot match a path that contains a colon, so a Windows absolute path like C:/repo/src/a.ts(3,5) is dropped. finding.title: quotePromptCommandArg escapes embedded quotes with backslash, which cmd.exe does not honor
finding.summary: quotePromptCommandArg claims its output is 'safe to paste into posix sh, PowerShell, and cmd', but it neutralizes an embedded double quote as \" — a convention cmd.exe's own command-line scanner does not implement (cmd has no backslash escape; the argv-level convention there is doubling, ""). A rendered command containing a quote therefore terminates its quoted region early under cmd.exe, splitting the argument and leaving the remainder subject to cmd metacharacter interpretation. entries.title: The tooling implementation_hash is ordered with localeCompare, so the same tree can hash differently across locales/ICU builds
entries.rationale: Finding excluded by the intent checkpoint (filter or excluded scope).

finding.title: The tooling implementation_hash is ordered with localeCompare, so the same tree can hash differently across locales/ICU builds
finding.summary: buildToolingManifest (src/audit/io/toolingManifest.ts:70-95) folds file paths and contents into a sha256 in the order produced by `files.sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b))` (line 81, and the same collation inside collectFiles at line 45). String.prototype.localeCompare is locale- and ICU-version-dependent: paths differing by case, punctuation (`-`, `_`, `.`) or non-ASCII characters can collate differently under a different default locale or a small-icu Node build, which permutes the hash input and yields a different implementation_hash for a byte-identical package. Because implementation_hash is the tool-identity input to staleness, a locale difference (or a Node upgrade changing ICU) manifests as a phantom tool change that invalidates downstream artifacts and forces expensive re-runs. Codepoint ordering (`a < b ? -1 : 1`) is the deterministic choice. The digest also concatenates path and content separated only by newlines with no length prefix, so a path/content pair containing newlines is not unambiguously framed.
evidence: src/audit/io/toolingManifest.ts:81 `for (const file of files.sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b)))` feeding the sha256 update order.
src/audit/io/toolingManifest.ts:45 `entries.sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))` — same locale-sensitive collation in the recursive walk.
src/audit/io/toolingManifest.ts:82-85 hash.update(path) + '\n' + hash.update(content) + '\n' — no length framing.
runtime:unit:src-audit: not_confirmed — Deterministic runtime command failed with exit code 1: npm test
reproduction: Compute buildToolingManifest() on a tree containing paths that collate differently under ICU vs codepoint order (e.g. `a-b.ts` and `ab.ts`), under two different default locales.
Compare implementation_hash between the two runs.

finding.title: Reflection NDJSON is validated by a hand-rolled parser that diverges from the declared zod schema (strictness silently lost)
finding.summary: `AgentReflectionSchema` is declared as the single source of the reflection shape and is `.strict()`, but `parseReflectionsNdjson` never calls it: it re-implements the checks by hand. The two disagree in ways that change what is accepted — the hand parser silently ACCEPTS objects with unknown extra keys (which `.strict()` rejects) and silently DROPS `ambiguities`/`tool_friction`/`suggestions` when they are arrays containing a non-string (zod would reject the record instead). So the exported type `AgentReflection` no longer describes what actually passed validation, and a worker's malformed-but-present friction list disappears from the aggregate with no signal at all. This is exactly the two-copies-of-one-rule pattern the repo bans; the schema is dead weight on the parse path.

finding.title: StepArtifactSchema is .strict() but the persisted step JSON always carries agent_id
finding.summary: src/audit/cli/steps.ts declares StepArtifactSchema with .strict() and derives StepArtifact from it, but every audit step contract is written by the shared writeStepContract, which unconditionally stamps agent_id onto the object it writes and returns. finding.title: stableStringify collapses Date/Map/Set (and any non-plain object) to identical output
finding.summary: The module is declared the ONE deterministic serializer for content hashing, but its object branch uses Object.entries, whose result is empty for Date, Map and Set. entries.title: git helpers parse path output without disabling core.quotepath, so non-ASCII paths come back C-quoted and never join to real files
entries.rationale: Finding excluded by the intent checkpoint (filter or excluded scope).

finding.title: git helpers parse path output without disabling core.quotepath, so non-ASCII paths come back C-quoted and never join to real files
finding.summary: Every git path reader in src/shared/git.ts (gitLines → changedFiles, fileCommits, stagedAndUntracked; and mineGitHistory's `git log --name-only`) consumes plain newline-separated output with no `-z` and no `-c core.quotepath=false`. Git's default (core.quotepath=true, unset in this checkout) emits any path containing a byte >0x7F — or a quote/backslash/control char — as a double-quoted, backslash-escaped literal such as `"src/caf\303\251.ts"`. Those strings are then treated as repo-relative paths: mineGitHistory keys churn/authorship/co-change on them, and changedFiles/stagedAndUntracked hand them to the delta-mode scope. They never match a real repo path, so history signals for such files are attributed to a phantom path and delta scoping silently omits the file. The module is otherwise carefully OS/encoding-agnostic, which makes this the one place a non-ASCII repo degrades wrongly rather than emptily.
evidence: src/shared/git.ts:12-17 — `runTracked(["git", ...args])` then `result.stdout.split(/\r?\n/)`; no `-z`, no `core.quotepath=false` anywhere in the file.
src/shared/git.ts:209-225 — the log invocation passes `--use-mailmap --max-count --no-merges --name-only --format=%H%x00%aN`; quoting is left at the git default.
`git config core.quotepath` in this repo returns nothing (unset ⇒ default true).
runtime:unit:src-shared: not_confirmed — Deterministic runtime command failed with exit code 1: npm test
reproduction: Commit a file whose path contains a non-ASCII character (e.g. `src/café.ts`).
Call mineGitHistory(root) — the churn/authorship entry's `path` is the quoted escape form, not `src/café.ts`, so it joins to nothing downstream.

entries.title: Access-memory recency silently assigns the OLDEST ordinal to an item whose block is missing from the plan
entries.rationale: Finding excluded by the intent checkpoint (filter or excluded scope).

finding.title: Access-memory recency silently assigns the OLDEST ordinal to an item whose block is missing from the plan
finding.summary: deriveRemediationAccessMemory resolves an item's recency ordinal with `ordinalByBlock.get(item.block_id) ?? 0` (accessMemory.ts:57). Ordinal 0 is the FIRST (oldest) block in the (phase_ordinal, block_id) ordering, so an item whose block_id is absent from state.plan.blocks — a replanned run, or a state whose plan was rewritten while items survived — is attributed the least-recent position rather than being detected or excluded. Since recency is `last_ordinal / total_ordinals` and drives the continuity bias in computeBlockContinuityScores, the mis-attribution quietly de-prioritizes exactly the files an orphaned item edited, and no diagnostic is emitted. The same lookup gap also silently yields an empty edit surface via `blockById.get(item.block_id)?.touched_files ?? []` when the item carries no item_spec.
evidence: src/remediate/state/accessMemory.ts:45-46 ordinalByBlock/blockById built only from state.plan.blocks
src/remediate/state/accessMemory.ts:57 `?? 0` fallback maps an unknown block to the oldest ordinal
src/remediate/state/accessMemory.ts:58-61 touched_files fallback degrades to an empty surface

reproduction: Build a RemediationState whose items reference a block_id not present in plan.blocks; the derived AccessMemory records those paths at ordinal 0 with no warning

entries.title: Lane-id lookup walks the prototype chain, so lanes named after Object.prototype members resolve to a non-schema and crash the validator

finding.title: Lane-id lookup walks the prototype chain, so lanes named after Object.prototype members resolve to a non-schema and crash the validator
finding.summary: laneSubmissionValidator indexes the plain object literal LANE_SUBMISSION_SCHEMAS with an arbitrary caller-supplied lane string. Because the literal inherits from Object.prototype, a lane id such as 'constructor', 'toString', 'valueOf' or 'hasOwnProperty' yields a truthy inherited value that is not a zod schema; the function then returns a validator that calls schema.safeParse(...) on it, throwing a TypeError instead of returning the documented null 'unknown lane -> refuse' signal. The module's own doc comment states that an unknown lane must be refusable ('no contract must never read as passes'), and the recovery verb is an explicitly second, operator-driven reader of this table — exactly the path where an unvetted lane string arrives.
evidence: src/audit/cli/laneValidators.ts:124 — `export const LANE_SUBMISSION_SCHEMAS: Readonly<Record<string, ZodTypeAny>> = { ... }` is a plain object literal (no `Object.create(null)`, no `Map`).

src/audit/cli/laneValidators.ts:176-177 — `const schema = LANE_SUBMISSION_SCHEMAS[lane]; if (schema) return (value) => schemaIssue(schema, value);` — a truthiness test on a prototype-chain lookup, with no own-property check.
src/audit/cli/laneValidators.ts:133-135 — `schemaIssue` immediately calls `schema.safeParse(value)`, which is absent on `Object.prototype` members such as `toString`/`constructor`.
src/audit/cli/laneValidators.ts:166-171 — the contract comment requires `null` for a lane 'not one this tool knows', which this path cannot deliver for inherited keys.

finding.title: Version bump is not rolled back when the release commit/tag step fails, leaving a dirty tree with an unreleased version
finding.summary: bumpVersionAndTag() mutates package.json/package-lock.json via `npm version --no-git-tag-version` and only then runs `git add`, `git commit` and `git tag`. Each of those goes through run(), which throws on any non-zero exit. There is no try/finally or rollback, so a failure at add/commit/tag (e.g. package-lock.json absent or unstageable, a commit hook refusal, or a tag name that already exists from a previously deleted release) aborts the script with the working tree already bumped. finding.title: computeCriticalPathMs memoizes cycle-truncated totals, so a cyclic needs graph yields silently wrong critical-path numbers
finding.summary: walk() guards recursion with a `visiting` set and, on re-entry, returns the node's own self-duration instead of its total. finding.title: getDefaultBranch builds a RegExp from the remote name without escaping it
finding.summary: The symbolic-ref branch strips the remote prefix with `new RegExp(\`^refs/remotes/${remoteName}/\`)`. remoteName comes from `git remote` output and is not escaped, so any regex metacharacter a git remote name legally permits (`.` and `+` are both valid in remote names) is interpreted as a pattern. finding.title: rebaseRelativeLinks silently leaves a link untouched when its target contains a space or parenthesis
finding.summary: The inline-link rewriter matches the target with `([^)<>\s]+)`, so a markdown target containing a space (`[t](../a b.md)`), a parenthesis (`[t](../a(1).md)`) or an angle-bracketed target with spaces never matches the pattern and is copied verbatim into the destination document. finding.title: Non-ENOENT IO errors on gate lanes abort next-step but do not destroy sibling data
finding.summary: The `tryConsumeSubmission` function explicitly re-throws every IO error that is neither a missing-file (ENOENT-family) nor a JsonParseError. This behavior is documented in its function contract and is a deliberate design choice. While this aborts the entire `next-step` call, it does not destroy sibling lane data. Each lane's submission file is unlinked ONLY after its content is persisted (e.g., after `design_assessment.json` is written and the pass snapshot is captured). Thus, no consumed-but-not-yet-persisted results are lost, and the next invocation re-consumes both lanes.

 * never a name a host could type. `ok` when the file exists and parses;
 * `absent` on ENOENT-family errors; `malformed` when the file exists but is not
 * JSON — submitted content is the CALLER's to quarantine, never an
 * infrastructure failure. All other IO errors re-throw unchanged.
 */

finding.impact: Availability impact only: an unreadable path at one lane wedges every `next-step` call until the operator clears it. There is no lane-scoped diagnostic, and the behavior is not surfaced as a resumable error.

finding.summary: Deepening verdict on nsh-correctness-001: the MECHANISM stands but the IMPACT does not. tryConsumeSubmission does re-throw every non-ENOENT, non-JsonParseError IO failure (EISDIR/EACCES/EBUSY), and handleDesignReviewBranch consumes the contract lane before the conceptual lane, so such an error aborts next-step before the second lane is read. But the propagation is an explicit, documented design choice in two places, and the claimed consequence — destroying a sibling lane's consumed-but-not-yet-persisted results — is refuted by the code: consumption is a pure read, and each lane's submission file is unlinked ONLY after design_assessment.json is written and the pass snapshot captured, so an abort loses nothing and the next invocation re-consumes both lanes. Residual real issue is availability only: an unreadable path at one lane wedges every next-step call until the operator clears it, with no lane-scoped diagnostic. Recommend severity high -> low and confidence high -> medium.

finding.summary: chunking.ts:17-21 advances the cursor with `end = Math.min(start + chunkSize - 1, totalLines); start = end + 1`. finding.title: Completed lanes are re-declared to recordExpectedLanes, so an accepted lane is re-owed and re-logged on every emission
finding.summary: materializeFanoutLanes computes resultExists per lane and uses it to build pendingLanes, but the set handed to recordExpectedLanes is filtered ONLY by spec.expected !== false (lines 140-146) — completed lanes are still declared as owed. recordLaneOutcome (laneSubmissions.ts:489-495) removes an ACCEPTED lane's submission id from the persisted expected set; the very next emission of the same fan-out re-declares that lane, mergeExpectedSets classifies it as newly added, so it is written back into the expected set as owed again AND another kind:"expected" ledger event is appended. Filtering the declared set by lane.resultExists (or by the persisted acceptance) would make the record match its stated meaning.

finding.title: The minting chokepoint enforces no uniqueness on lane id or promptFilename despite the documented invariant
finding.summary: The FanoutLaneSpec doc (lines 34-45) states the lane id "must be unique across the whole audit", and the module presents itself as the minting CHOKEPOINT where a host-typed filename is not expressible. But materializeFanoutLanes performs no uniqueness check on spec.id or spec.promptFilename. Two specs sharing an id derive the same resultPath (laneSubmissionPath is deterministic in the lane id alone) and collide on the artifactPaths keys `${id}_prompt` / `${id}_results` (lines 150-153), so the map silently holds one entry for two lanes, one submission satisfies both, and readPaths/writePaths contain duplicates.
